Tamales Oaxaqueños

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 8-10Prep 1 hourCook 1 hour 30 minutes

Tamales Oaxaqueños are a traditional Mexican dish from the Oaxaca region, often served during Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation) on February 2nd. This holiday marks the end of the Christmas season, and families gather to share tamales wrapped in banana leaves, symbolizing warmth and togetherness.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 3 cups chicken broth, warm
  • 1 1/2 cups lard or vegetable shortening, softened
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 2 cups cooked shredded chicken
  • 2 cups mole negro sauce (traditional Oaxacan black mole)
  • Banana leaves, cleaned and cut into 10x10 inch (25x25 cm) squares, softened by steaming or heating
  • Kitchen twine or strips of banana leaf for tying

Method

  1. Soften the banana leaves by steaming or heating until pliable; cut into squares about 10x10 inches (25x25 cm).
  2. In a large bowl, beat the lard or shortening until fluffy.
  3. In a separate bowl, mix the masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
  4. Gradually add the masa mixture to the lard, alternating with warm chicken broth, and beat until the dough is light and spreadable.
  5. Spread a thin layer of masa dough onto the center of each banana leaf square.
  6. Add a spoonful of shredded chicken on top of the masa.
  7. Top the chicken with a generous spoonful of mole negro sauce.
  8. Fold the banana leaf over the filling to form a square package and tie securely with kitchen twine or strips of banana leaf.
  9. Place the tamales standing upright in a large steamer pot with water below the rack.
  10. Steam the tamales for about 1 hour and 30 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure the water does not evaporate.
  11. Remove tamales from the steamer and let them rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • If banana leaves are unavailable, corn husks can be used as a substitute, though the flavor differs.
  • For a vegetarian version, replace chicken with sautéed mushrooms or beans and use a vegetarian mole sauce.
  • Ensure the masa dough is light and fluffy by properly beating the lard and incorporating air for the best texture.
